Seven: His saying: ﴿We will make you recite, and you will not forget﴾ [Al-A'la: 6].

As for the Sunnah, it is what is reported from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzaymah, that he was asked about this story and said: This is a fabrication of the heretics (zanadiqah), and he wrote a book on it. Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Bayhaqi said: This story is not established in terms of transmission. He then began discussing that the narrators of this story are impugned. Also, al-Bukhari reported in his Sahih that "the Prophet, peace be upon him, recited Surah al-Najm and the Muslims, the polytheists, humans and jinn prostrated in it," and there is nothing in it about the story of the cranes. This hadith has been reported through many routes, and none of them at all contains the story of the cranes.

As for reason, there are several points:

One: Whoever permits for the Messenger (ﷺ) the glorification of idols has disbelieved, because it is known by necessity that the greatest of his striving was in negating idols.

Two: At the beginning he (ﷺ) could not pray and recite the Qur'an at the Ka'bah safe from the harm of the polytheists, who at times would stretch their hands toward him. He would only pray when they were not present, at night or in times of solitude, and this invalidates their claim.

Three: Their hostility toward the Messenger was too great for them to acknowledge this degree of recitation without first ascertaining the reality of the matter. How then did they all agree that he glorified their gods, to the point that they fell down prostrating, when he had not shown them agreement with them?

Four: His saying: ﴿So God abrogates what Satan casts, then God makes His verses firm﴾. The making firm of the verses by removing what Satan casts upon the Messenger is stronger than abrogating them with these verses in which doubt remains. So if God wills to make the verses firm lest what is not Qur'an be mixed with the Qur'an, then that Satan be prevented from this altogether is more fitting.

Five, which is the strongest of the points: If we permitted that, the security of His law would be lifted, and we would permit that each of the rulings and laws could be like that, and His saying would be invalidated: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord; and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message; and God will protect you from the people﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 67]. For in reason there is no difference between a deficiency in revelation and an addition to it.

By these points we know, in general terms, that this story is fabricated. At most, a group of commentators mentioned it, but they did not reach the level of mass transmission (tawatur), and a single report (khabar al-wahid) does not oppose the textual and rational proofs that are mass-transmitted.

Now let us begin the detailed discussion. We say: The word tamanni (wishing) comes in the language with two meanings: One: the wishing of the heart. Two: recitation. God said: ﴿Among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Book except as wishes (amani)﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 78], meaning except as recitation, because the unlettered one does not know the Qur'an from the written copy, but knows it only by recitation. Hassan said:

"He wished for the Book of God at the first night and its last, and met the death-decree of the fates."

It was said: Recitation was only called "wish" (umniyyah) because the reciter, when he reaches a verse of mercy, wishes to attain it, and when he reaches a verse of punishment, wishes not to be afflicted by it. Abu Muslim said: Tamanni means taqdir (determining, decreeing), and tamanna is a form of tafa''ala from muniytu, and al-maniyyah is a person's death at the time God has decreed; and "manaa Allah laka" means God decreed for you. The transmitters of the language said: al-umniyyah means recitation, and they argued with Hassan's verse; this returns to the root we have mentioned, for the reciter determines the letters and mentions them one by one. The summary of this discussion is that al-umniyyah is either recitation or a passing thought.

If we interpret it as recitation, there are two views. The first: God intended by it what the Messenger (ﷺ) might err in, and what might be confused for the reciter, not what they narrated from his saying, "Those are the exalted cranes." The second: The intended meaning is the occurrence of this phrase in his recitation. Then those who hold this view differed in several ways:

The first way: The Prophet (ﷺ) did not say "Those are the exalted cranes," nor did Satan say it, nor did anyone say it. Rather, when he (peace be upon him) recited Surah al-Najm, the matter became confused for the disbelievers, so they supposed that some of his words were what they narrated as their saying, "Those are the exalted cranes," and this is in accordance with the custom of mistaking some words for something other than what is being said. This view was held by a group, and it is weak for several reasons.

[p. 46]

The first point: such a delusion can only occur regarding something that people are accustomed to hearing. As for what has not been heard, such a delusion does not arise concerning it. Second: even if it were so, this delusion would have affected some of the listeners and not others, since custom prevents a large crowd from all agreeing, at the same moment, on one false imagining about things perceived by the senses. Third: if it were so, it would not be attributed to Satan.

The second aspect: They said that this utterance was the speech of a Satan of the jinn. This would be by uttering words of his own accord, inserting them during some pauses of that recitation so that they would be taken to be of the same kind as what was heard from the Messenger (ﷺ). They said: What confirms this is that there is no disagreement that the jinn and the devils speak, so there is nothing to prevent Satan from producing a voice like the voice of the Messenger, peace be upon him, and speaking these words in the midst of the Messenger's speech, during his silence. When those present heard that word in a voice like the Messenger's, and did not see another person, they supposed that it was the speech of the Messenger. Then this would not be damaging to prophethood, since it was not his action. This also is weak. For if you allow that Satan could speak in the midst of the speech of the Messenger (ﷺ) with words that would appear to all listeners to be the speech of the Messenger, this possibility would remain in everything the Messenger says, and it would lead to the removal of trust in the entire Shari'ah. If it is said: This possibility exists in everything, but if it had occurred, it would have been necessary, in the wisdom of God the Exalted, that the situation be explained, as in this incident, to remove the confusion. We reply: It is not obligatory upon God to remove all possibilities, as in the case of the ambiguous (mutashabihat) matters. And since it is not obligatory upon God to do that, the possibility is open for everything.

The third aspect: It is said that the one who spoke this was some of the devils of mankind, namely the disbelievers. When the Messenger (ﷺ) reached this place in the recitation of this surah and mentioned the names of their gods, and they knew from his habit that he would disparage them, one of those present said "tilka al-gharaniq al-ula" (those are the exalted cranes), and the matter became confused for the people because of the great noise and the loud clamor, and their seeking to refute him and to drown out his recitation. Perhaps this happened during his prayer, because they would come close to him during his prayer, listen to his recitation, and make noise during it. It was also said that when he (peace be upon him) recited the Qur'an to the Quraysh, he would pause between the verses, and one of those present threw that utterance into those pauses, so the people imagined it was part of the recitation of the Messenger (ﷺ). Then God the Exalted attributed that to Satan, because it comes about first through his whisperings, and because He (glory be to Him) made that speaker a Satan in himself. This also is weak, for two reasons:

The first: If it were so, it would have been obligatory upon the Messenger (ﷺ) to remove the doubt, to state the truth clearly, to rebuke that speaker, and to make known that this word had come from someone other than him.

The second: If he had done that, it would have been more worthy of being transmitted. If it is said: The Messenger (ﷺ) did not do that because he had already conveyed the surah in its entirety to the community without this addition, so this did not lead to confusion, just as his forgetfulness in prayer does not lead to confusion after he has finished it. We reply: The Qur'an was not fixed in one state during his lifetime, for verses would come to him and he would add them to their surahs. So conveying that surah without this addition was not a cause for removing the confusion. Moreover, if it were so, he would not have deserved the reproach from God the Exalted that the people have related.

The fourth aspect: The one who uttered this was the Messenger (ﷺ) himself. This has three possibilities: he said this word either through forgetfulness, or by compulsion, or by choice.

As for the first possibility, that he (peace be upon him) said this word through forgetfulness: as is related from Qatadah and Muqatil, they both said: He (peace be upon him) was praying near the Maqam, he dozed, and these two phrases slipped from his tongue. When he finished the surah, he prostrated, and everyone in the mosque prostrated. The polytheists rejoiced at what they had heard. Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and asked him to recite it, and when he reached "the exalted cranes" he said: "I did not bring you this." So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) grieved until this verse was revealed. This also is weak, for several reasons:

First: If this forgetfulness were permissible, it would be permissible in all other places, and in that case trust in the Shari'ah would disappear.

Second: The one who is forgetful cannot produce words like these, which conform to the meter of the surah, its manner, and its meaning. For we know by necessity that if someone were to recite a poem, it would not be possible for him to forget so that a line of poetry in its meter, meaning, and style occurs from him.

Third: Suppose he had spoken those words through forgetfulness. How was he not alerted to them when he recited them to Gabriel (peace be upon him)? This is evident.

As for the second possibility, that he (peace be upon him) spoke those words by compulsion, which is what some people said: that Satan forced the Prophet (ﷺ)

[p. 47]

to say these words. This too is invalid, for several reasons:

First: If Satan were able to do that to the Prophet (peace be upon him), his power over us would be even greater. Then Satan would be obliged to turn people away from the religion, and it would be permissible for most of what any one of us says to be the result of compulsion by the devils.

Second: If Satan were able to compel in this way, trust in revelation would be lost, because this possibility would remain.

Third: It is invalid according to the statement of God the Exalted, quoting Satan: "And I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves" (14:22). And He said: "Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord. His authority is only over those who take him as a friend" (16:100). And He said: "Except Your sincere servants among them" (15:40). And there is no doubt that he (peace be upon him) was the master of the sincere ones.

As for the third possibility, that he (peace be upon him) spoke those words by choice, then here there are two views: One is that we say this word is false. The other is that we say it is not a false word.

As for the first view, they mentioned two ways. The first: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, related through 'Ata', said: A devil called al-Abyad came to him in the form of Gabriel (peace be upon him), and cast this word upon him, and he recited it. When the polytheists heard that, it pleased them. Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) came and presented the surah to him, and he recited it. When he reached that word, Gabriel (peace be upon him) said: "I did not bring you this." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Someone came to me in your form and cast it upon my tongue." The second way: Some ignorant people said: Because of his intense eagerness for the faith of the people, he (peace be upon him) inserted this word from his own self, then he retracted it. Neither of these two opinions is desired by any Muslim at all. For the first implies that he (peace be upon him) did not distinguish between the infallible angel and the wicked devil, and the second implies that he was treacherous in revelation. Each of these is a departure from the religion.

As for the second view, that this word is not false, there are also several ways here. The first: It is said that "the cranes" are the angels, and that this was a Qur'an revealed in description of the angels. When the polytheists imagined that he meant their gods, God abrogated (naskh, the cancellation of a ruling or recitation) its recitation. The second: It is said that what is meant is a question in the form of denial, as if he had said: "Is their intercession hoped for?" The third: It is said that he mentioned an affirmation while meaning a negation, as in God's saying: "God makes clear to you lest you go astray" (4:176), meaning "lest you go astray." Just as a negation is sometimes mentioned while meaning an affirmation, as in God's saying: "Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you: that you should not associate anything with Him" (6:151), the meaning being "that you associate." Against these last two interpretations it is objected: If that were permissible according to this interpretation, why would it not be permissible for them to express a word of disbelief within the body of the Qur'an, or in prayer, according to this interpretation? But the principle regarding the religion is that nothing of that sort is permissible for them, because God the Exalted has appointed them as proofs and chosen them for the mission. So what would cast doubt on that or cause aversion is not permissible for them. And of such aversion, there is a greater degree in the matters from which God the Exalted urged him to refrain, such as harshness, writing, and the composition of poetry. So these views mentioned in his phrase "those are the exalted cranes" have clearly been shown to be false. All of this applies if we interpret the "tamanni" (wishing, reciting) as recitation. But if we interpret it as thought and the wish of the heart, the meaning is that whenever the Prophet (peace be upon him) wished for some of the things he desired, Satan would whisper falsehood to him, and call him to what is not fitting. Then God the Exalted would abrogate that and nullify it, and guide him to abandon paying attention to his whisperings. Then they differed about the manner of that whispering in several ways:

The first: He wished for what would bring him closer to the polytheists by praising their gods. They said: He (peace be upon him) loved to win them over, and he kept turning this over in his mind. When drowsiness overtook him, that addition was added from the place that was in his mind. This also is a departure from the religion, and its explanation has already been given.

[p. 48]

The second: What Mujahid said, that he (peace be upon him) wished for the revelation to descend upon him quickly without delay, so God abrogated that by informing him that its descent is according to the interests in events, occurrences, and other matters.

The third: It is possible that when revelation descended, he (peace be upon him) was reflecting on its interpretation, if it was ambiguous, so Satan cast into its content what he did not intend. Then God the Exalted made clear that He abrogates that by nullifying it, and establishes what God the Exalted intended by His proofs and signs.

The fourth: The meaning of the verse is: When he wishes (a deed), when he desires an act that brings him closer to God the Exalted, Satan casts into his thought what contradicts it, and he returns to God the Exalted regarding that. This is like God's saying: "Indeed, those who fear God, when a visitation from Satan touches them, remember, and then they are seeing clearly" (7:201), and like His saying: "And if a prompting from Satan should incite you, then seek refuge in God" (7:200).

Some people said: It is not permissible to interpret the "umniyya" (wish) as the wish of the heart, for if it were so, what came to the mind of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would not have been a trial for the disbelievers. And this is refuted by His saying: "That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is disease and whose hearts are hardened" (22:53). The answer: It is not far-fetched that when the wish is strong, the mind becomes occupied with it, so forgetfulness occurs in outward acts because of it, and that becomes a trial for the disbelievers. This is the end of what was said regarding this matter.

* * *

**The third issue:** The upshot of the discussion is that the purpose of this verse is to show that the Messengers whom God sent, although He protected them from error when they knowingly conveyed the message, did not protect them from the possibility of forgetfulness and the whisperings of Satan. Their situation regarding this possibility is like that of the rest of mankind. It is therefore obligatory that they be followed only in what they do knowingly, and that is the *muhkam* (the firm, clearly established). Abu Muslim said: the meaning of the verse is that He did not send a prophet except when he *tamanna* (wished or recited). It is as if it were said: "We did not send to mankind an angel, nor did We send to them a prophet except from among them. And We did not send a prophet who, while reciting the revelation, was free from the whisperings of Satan, and from Satan casting into his mind what contradicts the revelation and distracts him from memorizing it. Rather, God makes the Prophet firm in the revelation and in its memorization, and informs him of the correctness of that and of the falsehood of what comes from Satan." He said: What preceded in His saying, ﴿Say: O mankind, I am only a plain warner to you﴾ [al-Hajj: 49], strengthens this interpretation. It is as if He commanded him to say to the disbelievers: "I am a warner to you, but I am of mankind, not of the angels. God did not send someone like me as an angel; rather, He sent men, so Satan whispered to them." If it is said: "This is valid only if forgetfulness is not possible for the angels," we say: If the angels are of a greater rank than the prophets, then Satan's gaining power over the prophets through whispering does not necessitate his gaining power over the angels through whispering.

* * *

Know that when He, glorified is He, explained the state of this whispering, He followed it with two discussions.

**The first discussion:** the manner of its removal, which is His saying, ﴿Then God abrogates what Satan casts﴾. The intended meaning is its removal and the removal of its influence. This is *al-naskh al-lughawi* (abrogation in the linguistic sense, i.e., removal), not *al-naskh al-shar'i* (abrogation in the legal sense, used for rulings). As for His saying, ﴿then God makes His verses firm﴾: if *tamanna* is understood as recitation, then what is meant is the verses of the Qur'an. Otherwise, it is understood as the rulings of the proofs in which error is not possible.

**The second discussion:** He, the Exalted, explained the effect of that whispering. Then He, glorified is He, explained its effect first with regard to the disbelievers, and then with regard to the believers. As for the disbelievers, it is His saying, ﴿so that He may make what Satan casts a trial﴾. What is meant by this is the intensifying of their distance, because when the Messenger (ﷺ) appears to be confused in the Qur'an through forgetfulness, they must investigate that, in order to distinguish forgetfulness from deliberate intent, and to know that deliberate intent is correct while forgetfulness may not be correct.

As for His saying, ﴿for those in whose hearts is a disease and whose hearts are hardened﴾, there are two questions about it.

**The first question:** Why did He say, ﴿a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾? And why did He specify them with that answer? Because they, despite their disbelief, need that consideration, whereas the believers already knew this beforehand, so they do not need that consideration.

**The second question:** What is the disease of the heart? The answer: it is doubt and confusion, and these are the hypocrites, as He said, ﴿in their hearts is a disease﴾. As for those whose hearts are hardened, they are the polytheists who persist in their ignorance, outwardly and inwardly.

As for His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And indeed the wrongdoers are in far-off opposition﴾, He means that these hypocrites and polytheists. Its origin is *wa-innahum* (and indeed they), so the apparent noun was placed in the position of the pronoun, to pass judgment upon them as wrongdoers, opponents, antagonists, enemies and far removed, all alike.

As for the believers, it is His saying, ﴿and that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord﴾. Regarding the pronoun (*al-kināya*, the reference), there are three possibilities:

First: it refers to the abrogation of what Satan cast, according to al-Kalbi. Second: it refers to *al-haqq* (the truth), meaning the Qur'an, according to Muqatil. Third: the empowerment of Satan to make that casting is the truth. As for our view, this is because He, glorified and exalted is He, whatever He does, He has disposed of His dominion and His possession (*mulk* and *milk*, read with a *dammah* and a *kasrah* on the *mim*), so it is truth. As for the view of the Mu'tazila (the rationalist school), it is because He, glorified is He, is wise, so all His acts are correct. Then they believe in it, so their hearts *tukhbitu* (humble themselves) to Him, that is, they submit and are at rest, knowing that what has been decreed will occur and that each is made easy for what He created him for. ﴿And indeed God guides those who believe﴾ to interpret what is ambiguous in religion through correct interpretations, and to seek what is unclear in it from the *mujmal* (the general or ambiguous), which the firm foundations require, so that no bewilderment reaches them and no doubt afflicts them. It has been read as *la-hādin* (a guide) with tanwin.

When He, glorified is He, had explained the state of the disbelievers first, and then the state of the believers second, He returned to explaining the state of the disbelievers once more, saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it﴾, that is, about the Qur'an or about the Messenger. This indicates that the ages until the Hour is established are not free of those described thus.

As for His saying, the Exalted, ﴿until the Hour comes upon them suddenly﴾, that is, unexpectedly, without their perceiving it. Then He made the Hour the limit of their disbelief, and that they will believe at the signs of the Hour, under compulsion.

The meaning of "the barren day" (*al-yawm al-'aqim*) has been disputed, and there are two opinions about it:

One: it is the day of Badr. The day of battle was described as barren for four reasons:
First: the sons of women are killed on it, so they become as if they were barren women who never bore children. Second: the fighters are called "the sons of war," so when they are killed, the day of battle is described as barren figuratively. Third: it is the day without good in it. It is said: "a barren wind" when it does not produce rain nor fertilize trees. Fourth: it has no equal in the magnitude of its affair, and that is because of the fighting of the angels in it.

The second opinion: it is the Day of Resurrection. It was described as barren for several reasons:
First: they see no good in it. Second: there is no night in it, so it continues as a woman continues in idleness from childbearing. Third: every pregnant woman will deliver her burden on that day, so how could pregnancy occur in it? This opinion is more preferable, because it is not permissible for God the Exalted to say, ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease﴾ and the intended meaning to be the day of Badr, since it is known that they were in doubt after the day of Badr. If it is said: since He mentioned the Hour, if we take the barren day to mean the Day of Resurrection, there would be repetition. We say: this is not so, because the Hour is one of the preliminaries of the Resurrection, while the barren day is that very day. Moreover, even if the matter were as he said, it would not be repetition, because in the first He mentioned the Hour, and in the second He mentioned the punishment of that day. It is also possible that what is meant by the Hour is the time of each person's death, and by the punishment of a barren day, the Resurrection.

As for His saying, ﴿The dominion on that day belongs to God﴾, it is among the strongest indications that the barren day is that day. By this He means that there is no owner on that day except Him, unlike the days of this world, in which God has granted matters to others besides Him. He made clear that He is the judge between them, and there is no judge besides Him. That is a deterrent from disobeying Him. Then He explained how He will judge between them: He will bring the believers into the Gardens of Bliss, and the disbelievers into the humiliating punishment. The description of Paradise and Hell has already been given before. If it is asked: for which clause does the tanwin in *yawma'idhin* (on that day) substitute? We say: its estimate is: "the dominion belongs to God on the day when they believe," or "on the day when their doubt is removed," because of His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes upon them﴾.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 22, verse 58:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who emigrated for the cause of Allah and then were killed or died, Allah will surely provide for them a good provision. And indeed, Allah is the best of providers.﴾ ﴿He will surely admit them to an entrance which they will be pleased with. And indeed, Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.﴾ ﴿That [is so]. And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was harmed by and then is tyrannized, Allah will surely aid him. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.﴾ ﴿That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and because Allah is Hearing and Seeing.﴾ ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and that what they invoke other than Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Greatest.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned that sovereignty belongs to Him on the Day of Resurrection, and that He judges between them and admits the believers into the Gardens, He followed this with the mention of His generous promise to the emigrants (al-muhajirun), singling them out for mention to exalt their status. So the Mighty and Majestic One said: ﴿And those who emigrated﴾. The scholars differed about who is meant by this. Some said: it refers to those who emigrated to Madinah seeking to support the Messenger ﷺ and seeking nearness to Allah, exalted is He. Others said: rather, it refers to those who fought, and went out with the Messenger ﷺ or in his expeditions (sara'ya) to support the religion, and for this reason killing is mentioned after it. Among them are those who understood it to include both matters. They also differed from another angle. Some said: the intended group is a specific people. Mujahid narrated that it was revealed concerning groups who left Makkah for Madinah for emigration, and the polytheists followed them and fought them. However, the apparent sense of the speech is general.

Then, glorified and exalted is He, described them by their provision and their dwelling. As for the provision, it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah will surely provide for them a good provision. And indeed, Allah is the best of providers.﴾ On this there are issues:

**The first issue:** There is no doubt that the "good provision" is the bliss of Paradise. Al-Asamm said that it is knowledge and understanding, like the saying of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him: ﴿and He provided me from Himself with a good provision﴾ [Hud: 88]. That refers to this world, and in the Hereafter it is Paradise. Al-Kalbi said: a good provision, lawful, and it is the spoils of war (ghanimah). These two views are weak, because He made it a reward for their emigration in the cause of Allah after being killed or dying, and after these two, there is nothing but the bliss of Paradise.

* * *

[Page 51]

**The second issue:** The condition of avoiding major sins (al-kaba'ir) must be present in every promise in the Qur'an. For this emigrant, if he committed a major sin, his ruling would be subject to the Will (of Allah) according to our view, and he would be definitively removed from being worthy of Paradise according to the view of the Mu'tazilah (the Rationalist school). If it is said: What is his superiority over the rest of the believers in the promise, if it is as you have said? We say: Their superiority appears because their reward is greater, and Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest﴾ [al-Hadid: 10]. It is known that whoever emigrated with the Messenger ﷺ and left his homeland and family, to strengthen him and support his religion, while the disbelievers were very powerful and their assault was evident, his act became like a cause for the strength of the religion. On this basis, the station of the Helpers (al-Ansar) became great, to the point that their mention and praise came right after the mention of the emigrants, because they sheltered him and supported him.

* * *

**The third issue:** They differed about the meaning of His saying: ﴿And indeed, Allah is the best of providers﴾, along with the knowledge that all provision is from Him, in several ways:

One of them: the difference only arises from the fact that He, glorified is He, is specifically able to provide what no one else is able to provide.

Second: that it means He is the origin of provision, and others only provide by means of what has already come from Allah, exalted is He.

Third: that another only transfers provision from his hand to the hand of another, not that he creates the provision itself.

Fourth: that when another provides, he provides for his own benefit, either to be free of an obligation, or to earn praise or commendation, or to relieve a natural human tenderness. So when one of us provides, he seeks a return. As for the Truthful One, glorified is He, His perfection is an essential attribute of His, so He does not gain any additional perfection from anything. Thus the provision that proceeds from Him is purely out of benevolence.

Fifth: that another only provides if the desire for that act arises in his heart, and that desire is from Allah. So the true provider is in reality Allah, exalted is He.

Sixth: that the one who is provided for is under the obligation (minnah) of the provider, and the obligation of Allah, exalted is He, is easier to bear than the obligation of another. So He is the ﴿best of providers﴾.

Seventh: that when another is provided for, were it not that Allah, exalted is He, had given that person kinds of senses, and given him soundness, health, and the ability to benefit from that provision, he would not be able to benefit from it. The provision of another must be preceded by the provision of Allah and followed by it, until benefit is achieved. As for the provision of Allah, exalted is He, He has no need for the provision of another. Thus it is established that He, glorified is He, is ﴿the best of providers﴾.

* * *

**The fourth issue:** The Mu'tazilah said: The verse indicates three matters:

One of them: that Allah, exalted is He, is capable.

Second: that other than Allah can provide and own, and were it not that he is capable and an agent, that would not be valid.

Third: that provision is only lawful, because His saying ﴿the best of providers﴾ is an indication that they are praiseworthy.

The response: There is no dispute that the servant is capable, for in our view, capability together with the motive is effective in the act, in the sense of necessitation (al-istilzam). As for the third, it is a verbal discussion, and the discussion of it has already passed.

**The fifth issue:** When He, exalted is He, said: ﴿then were killed or died﴾, equating the two in the promise, some people thought that the state of one killed in jihad and the one who dies on his bed is equal. If they took this from the apparent meaning, there is no evidence in it, because combining the two in the promise does not indicate preference or equality, just as combining the believers does not indicate that. If they took it from another proof, then it is true, for Anas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The one killed in the cause of Allah, exalted is He, and the one who dies in the cause of Allah without being killed, both are partners in good and reward." The word "partnership" (shirkah) indicates equality, otherwise there would be no benefit in singling out the two for mention. It is also narrated: "That groups of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said: O Messenger of Allah, these who were killed, we know what good Allah has given them, and we strive along with you as they strove. So what will there be for us if we die with you?" So Allah, exalted is He, revealed these two verses. This indicates equality, because when they asked about the measure of the reward, without equality the answer would not have been meaningful.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 22, verses 59–60:

As for the place (al-maskan), His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He will certainly admit them to an entrance which they will be pleased with. And indeed, Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.﴾ On this there are several issues:

page 52
The first issue: It has been recited as mudkhalan (with a ḍammah on the mīm), which is from al-idkhāl (admission). As for the one who recites it with a fatḥah, the meaning is the place (al-mawḍiʿ).

The second issue: It has been said regarding the entrance with which they will be pleased that it is a tent of white pearl, without any crack or flaw, having seventy thousand leaves (miṣrāʿ) of doors. Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī said: it is that He admits them to Paradise without any previous hardship. Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: He only said "with which they will be pleased" because they will see in Paradise what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, so they will be pleased with it and will not desire any alternative to it. Its parallels are His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and dwellings you are pleased with﴾ [al-Tawbah: 24], His saying: ﴿in a pleasing life﴾ [al-Ḥāqqah: 21], His saying: ﴿Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]﴾ [al-Fajr: 28], and His saying: ﴿and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence; and approval from Allah is greater﴾ [al-Tawbah: 72].

The third issue: If it is said: What is the meaning of ﴿And indeed, Allah is Knowing and Forbearing﴾? And what is its connection to what preceded? We say: It may be that He is Knowing of what they deserve, so He does it for them and increases it for them. It may also be that the meaning is that He is Knowing of what they are pleased with, so He gives them that in Paradise. As for al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing), the meaning is that, by His forbearance, He does not hasten punishment against the one who commits disobedience, but gives respite so that repentance may occur from him, and so he deserves Paradise from Him.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 22, verses 61–65:

Regarding His words: ﴿That is so. And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with, and then is wronged again, Allah will surely help him. Indeed Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾, there are several issues.

**The first issue:** His words ﴿That is so﴾. The discussion of this has already passed in this verse of this surah. Al-Zajjaj (d. 311 AH) said: "That is the matter, what We have related to you of fulfilling the promise to the emigrants who were killed or died."

**The second issue:** His words ﴿That is so. And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with, and then is wronged﴾ mean: he fought the one who had been fighting him, and then the fighter became the one wronged, in that he was compelled to emigrate and leave his homeland, and fighting was initiated against him. Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning a people from the polytheists who met a people from the Muslims for two nights remaining of Muharram (the sacred month). Some of them said to others: "The companions of Muhammad dislike fighting in the sacred month, so attack them." The Muslims appealed to them to refrain from fighting them out of respect for the sacred month, but they refused and fought them. That was their transgression against them, and the Muslims stood firm against them and were given victory over them. Then what happened happened in the hearts of the Muslims regarding fighting in the sacred month, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, pardoned them and forgave them.

Here there are questions:

**The first question:** What is the connection of this verse with what precedes it? The answer: It is as if He, glorified and exalted, said: "Along with My honoring them in the Hereafter through this promise, I will not leave off their support in this world against those who transgress against them."

**The second question:** Does this refer to the emigrants specifically, or to them and to the believers in general? The answer: The closer view is that it refers to both groups, since both have been mentioned before. This is clarified by His words ﴿Allah will surely help him﴾, and after being killed or dying, that is not possible in this world.

**The third question:** What is meant by the punishment mentioned? The answer: There are two views.

The first: What is meant is what the polytheists of Makkah did to the emigrants in Makkah, such as pursuing their traces and turning some of them back, and other things. So He, exalted is He, made clear that whoever retaliates against these disbelievers with the like of what they did, He will help him against them. This mentioned help strengthens the interpretation of those who understood it as fighting the disbelievers, not as retaliation (qisas), since the apparent sense of the text fits only that.

The second answer: This verse concerns retaliation (qisas) and wounds, and it is a Madani verse according to al-Dahhak.

**The fourth question:** Why did He call the initial act of theirs a "punishment"? The answer: The name of punishment was applied to the first act because of the connection between it and the second, as in His words ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [al-Shura: 40] and ﴿They deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them﴾ [al-Nisa: 142].

**The fifth question:** What is the connection of His words ﴿Indeed Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾ with what has preceded? The answer has several aspects.

First: Allah, exalted is He, urged the one who punishes toward pardoning the offender, by His words ﴿But whoever forgives and reconciles, his reward is with Allah﴾ [al-Shura: 40], ﴿And that you pardon is nearer to righteousness﴾ [al-Baqarah: 237], and ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [al-Shura: 43]. So when he did not do this recommended act, it is a kind of wrongdoing, and it is as if He, glorified is He, said: "I have pardoned this wrong and forgiven it, for I am the One who permitted you to do it."

Second: Although He, glorified is He, guaranteed him victory over the transgressor, He nonetheless alluded, along with that, to what was more fitting for him, namely pardon and forgiveness, and so He hinted at these two attributes.

Third: By mentioning pardon and forgiveness, He, glorified is He, indicated that He is able to punish, because one is not described as pardoning except one who is capable of the opposite.

**The sixth question:** What is the connection of His words ﴿That is so, because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night﴾ with what precedes it? The answer has two aspects.

First: "That" means: that victory is because He is Able, and among the signs of His far-reaching power is that He created the night and the day and directs them. Therefore He must be Knowing and Able over what occurs within them, and when He is like this, He is able to grant victory and is right in doing so.

Second: The intended meaning is that, glorified is He, along with that victory, bestows favor in this world through what He does by way of the succession of night and day and the entry of each into the other.

**The seventh question:** What is the meaning of the entry of night into day and the entry of day into night? The answer: There are two views.

The first: The darkness of this one occurs in the place of the light of that one by the setting of the sun, and the light of that one occurs in the place of the darkness of this one by its rising, just as a house is lit by a lamp and becomes dark when it is removed.

The second: He, glorified is He, adds to one of them what is lost from the other in hours.

**The eighth question:** What is the connection of His words ﴿And that Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾ with what has preceded? The answer: What is meant is that just as He is able to do what others cannot, so He perceives what is heard and what is seen, and it is not permissible to prevent Him from this. This works as a warning against undertaking what is impermissible regarding what is heard and seen.

**The ninth question:** What is the meaning of His words ﴿That is so, because Allah is the Truth﴾, and what is its connection with what has preceded? The answer: There are two views.

The first: What is meant is that the attribute mentioned before, of power over these matters, has come about only because Allah is the Truth, that is, He is the Existent who is Necessary in Himself, for whom change and cessation are impossible, and therefore He surely brought the promise and the threat.

The second: What is done in worshipping Him is the Truth, and what is done in worshipping other than Him is falsehood, as He said: ﴿He has no call in this world or in the Hereafter﴾ [Ghafir: 43].

**The tenth question:** What is the connection of His words ﴿And that Allah is the Exalted, the Great﴾ with what has preceded? The answer: "Exalted" means the Dominant, the Powerful, the One who cannot be overcome. By this He draws attention to the fact that He is the One able to harm and benefit, not any of the others who are worshipped, encouraging worship of Him and deterring from worship of others. As for "Great," it means magnificent in His power and sovereignty, and this also conveys the perfection of power.

[p. 54]

**The third issue:** His words ﴿Allah will surely help him﴾ are a report of the unseen, for its informant was found to be as he reported, and so it is one of the miracles.

**The fourth issue:** Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Whoever burns [someone], we burn him; whoever drowns [someone], we drown him." Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Rather, he is killed by the sword." Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) argued from this verse, for Allah, exalted is He, permitted the wronged person to punish with the like of what was done to him, and promised him victory in it.

**The fifth issue:** Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read ﴿tad'una﴾ (تَدْعُونَ) with the tā' here, and in Luqman, in al-Mu'minun, and in al-'Ankabut. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read all of them with the yā' (يَدْعُونَ), as reporting. The Arabs do shift from address to report and from report to address.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 22, verse 66:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allah is Subtle, All-Aware.﴾ ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ ﴿Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you whatever is on the earth, and the ships that sail upon the sea by His command, and He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission? Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to mankind.﴾ ﴿And it is He who gave you life, then causes you to die, then gives you life again. Indeed, man is ungrateful.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, had previously pointed to His power by what He mentioned of the entering of the night into the day, and drew attention thereby to His blessings, He followed it with other kinds of proofs of His power and His blessing, and they are six:

The first of them: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allah is Subtle, All-Aware.﴾ In it there are issues:

The first issue: They mentioned, regarding His saying ﴿Have you not seen﴾, three aspects:

One of them: that what is meant is the literal seeing, they said: because the water descending from the sky is seen with the eye, and the greening of the plants upon the earth is visible; and when it is possible to carry the speech upon its literal meaning, that is preferable. The second: that what is meant is "Have you not been informed," in the form of a question. The third: what is meant is "Have you not known" (ʿilm). The first opinion is weak, because although the water is visible, the fact that Allah is the One who sends it down from the sky is not visible. Once this is established, it is obligatory to interpret it as knowledge, because the purpose of that seeing is knowledge; for when seeing is not accompanied by knowledge, it is as though it had not occurred.

The second issue: It was read as ﴿mukhḍarra₩﴾ like *mabqala* and *masbaʿa* (meaning: possessing greenness), and here there are questions:

[Page 55]

The first question: Why did He say ﴿fa-tuṣbiḥu﴾ (the earth becomes) and not say *fa-aṣbahat*? The answer: there is a subtle point in it, which is conveying that the effect of the rain remains over time after time, as you say: "So-and-so bestowed a favour upon me in such-and-such a year, so I go forth and return thankful to him"; and if you said: "I rejoiced and I went forth," it would not occupy that position.

The second question: Why is it in the nominative and not in the accusative, as an answer to the interrogative? The answer: if it were in the accusative, it would give the opposite of the intended meaning; because its meaning is the affirmation of the greening, so by the accusative it would turn into the negation of the greening. An example of this: you say to your companion: "Have you not seen that I have bestowed favour upon you so that you give thanks?" If you put it in the accusative, you are negating his thanks and complaining of his negligence; and if you put it in the nominative, you are affirming thanks.

The third question: Why did He, exalted is He, cite this as a proof of His power over resurrection, as Abu Muslim said? The answer: this is possible, and it is also possible that He drew attention thereby to the greatness of His power and the vastness of His blessings.

The fourth question: What is the connection of His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle, All-Aware﴾ to what preceded? The answer: there are several aspects:

One of them: He intended that He is merciful to His servants, and out of His mercy He did that until their benefit from it became great; for when the earth becomes green and the sky sends down rain, that becomes a cause for the living of animals in all their varieties. The meaning of ﴿Aware﴾ is that He knows the measures of their interests, so He acts according to that measure without excess or deficiency. The second: Ibn ʿAbbas said: ﴿Subtle﴾ with the provisions of His servants, ﴿Aware﴾ of what is in their hearts of despair. The third: al-Kalbi said: ﴿Subtle﴾ in His acts, ﴿Aware﴾ of the deeds of His creation. The fourth: Muqatil said: ﴿Subtle﴾ in bringing forth the plant, ﴿Aware﴾ of the manner of its creation.

The second proof: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ The meaning is that all of that is subservient to Him, not resisting His disposal of it, and He is free of need from all things and also from the praise of those who praise Him; for He is perfect in His essence, and the one who is perfect in His essence is free of need from everything other than Himself in all matters. However, when He created the living creatures, wisdom necessitated rain and plants, so He created these things as mercy for the animals and as a favour upon them, not because He had any need for that. Since it is so, His bestowal is free of any purpose returning to Him, and so He deserves praise. It is as though He said: since He is free of need, He did not do what He did except for benevolence, and whoever is like that deserves praise, so it is necessary that He be Praiseworthy. Therefore He said: ﴿And indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾

The third proof: His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you whatever is on the earth﴾, that is, He made submissive to you what is in it; there is nothing harder than stone, nor sharper than iron, nor more awe-inspiring than fire, and He has subjected them to you. He has also subjected the animals, so that they may be benefited from in terms of eating, riding, carrying loads upon them, and benefiting by looking at them. Had Allah, exalted is He, not subjected camels and cattle despite their strength, so that the weak among people could tame them and have power over them, that would not have been a blessing.

The fourth proof: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and the ships that sail upon the sea by His command﴾. The closer view is that what is meant is: He subjected the ships for you to sail upon the sea. The manner of His subjecting the ships is that He subjected the water and the winds for their running; for had their characteristics not been as they are, they would not run, but would sink, stand still, or be wrecked. Thereby He, exalted is He, drew attention to His blessings in this, and in that He created what ships are made from, and in that He explained how they are made. He said "by His command" only because, since He is the One who makes them run by the winds, He attributed that to His command in a broader sense; for that conveys His exaltation more than if He had attributed it to an act, following the custom of kings in such an expression.

The fifth proof: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission. Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to mankind.﴾

[Page 56]

﴿Merciful﴾. Know that the blessings mentioned earlier are not complete except by this one; for the sky is the dwelling of the angels, so it must be solid, and it must be heavy, and whatever is so must fall unless something prevents it. This argument is based on the apparent notions. As for His saying ﴿lest it fall﴾ (anna taqaʿa): the Kufans said: "lest it fall" (kay lā taqaʿa), and the Basrans said: "out of aversion that it fall" (karāhiyata an taqaʿa). This is based on a theological question, namely whether volitions and aversions relate to non-existence. Whoever denies that goes to the first interpretation, and the meaning is that He held it back so that it would not fall, lest the blessings He bestowed be nullified.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to mankind﴾, the meaning is that the Bestower of these comprehensive blessings for the benefits of this world and the next has reached the utmost in goodness and bestowal; so He is, therefore, Kind and Merciful.

The sixth proof: His saying: ﴿And it is He who gave you life, then causes you to die, then gives you life again. Indeed, man is ungrateful.﴾ The meaning is that the One who subjected these matters to him and bestowed these blessings upon him is the One who gave him life. By the first giving of life He drew attention to the worldly favours bestowed upon us through all that has been mentioned. By the death and the second giving of life He drew attention to the blessings of religion upon us; for indeed He, glorified and exalted is He, created the world with all its states for the sake of the Hereafter, otherwise the blessings would have no meaning in this respect. This is shown by the fact that, were it not for the matter of the Hereafter, there would be no meaning to cultivating crops and bearing their cost, nor to riding animals and slaughtering them and so on; rather, He would create it from the outset without the toil of sowing and irrigating. Allah only made this custom so that a lesson might be drawn from it in matters of religion. When He, exalted is He, had detailed these blessings, He said: ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful﴾. This is like a man who enumerates his blessings upon his child and then says: "Indeed, the child is ungrateful for the father's blessings," as a rebuke to him against ingratitude and an incitement to him to give thanks. Therefore He, exalted is He, mentioned this regarding the disbelievers, and He made clear that they rejected these blessings, disbelieved in them, and ignored their Creator despite the clarity of the matter. A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And few of My servants are grateful﴾ [Saba': 13]. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "Man" here means the disbeliever. He also said: it is al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, Abu Jahl, al-ʿAs, and Ubayy ibn Khalaf. The preferable view is to generalise it to all who deny.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 22, verses 67–70:**

The words of the Exalted: ﴿For every community We have appointed a rite (mansak), which they perform. So let them not dispute with you over the matter, and invite to your Lord. Indeed you are upon a straight guidance.﴾ ﴿And if they argue with you, say: "Allah knows best what you do."﴾ ﴿Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which you used to differ.﴾

Know that when the Exalted had mentioned His blessings and shown that He is Compassionate and Merciful to His servants, even though some of them disbelieve and do not give thanks, He followed this with mention of the blessings of what He has prescribed, saying: ﴿For every community We have appointed a rite which they perform.﴾ On this there are several issues:

**The first issue:** He omitted the conjunction "wa" (and) in His words ﴿For every community﴾ because this statement has no connection with what precedes it, so He therefore dropped the connecting particle.

**The second issue:** There are several opinions regarding the word *mansak* (rite). First: Ibn ʿAbbas said, "a festival (ʿīd) on which they slaughter." Second: a sacrifice (qurbān); the word *mansak* is specific to sacrificial animals, according to Mujahid. Third: a place they are accustomed to, either a specific place or a specific time, for performing acts of worship. Fourth: *mansak* means the sacred law (sharīʿa) and the path (minhāj). This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas as transmitted by ʿAtaʾ, and it was chosen by al-Qaffal, and it is the closest of these opinions, because of the Exalted's words: ﴿For each of you We have appointed a law and a path﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48]. Also, *mansak* is derived from *nusk*, which means worship, and when the term applies to every act of worship, there is no reason to restrict it. If it is said: "Why not take it to mean slaughter, since in common usage *mansak* is understood only as slaughter? Or why not take it to mean the place of worship or its time?" The answer to the first: We do not concede that in common usage *mansak* is restricted to slaughter. The proof of this is that all the acts performed in the Hajj are described as *manāsik* (rites), and for this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Take your rites (*manāsikakum*) from me." The answer to the second: His words ﴿they perform it﴾ are more suited to worship than to time and place.

**The third issue:** Some people claimed that the intended meaning of His words ﴿they perform it﴾ is those who, at the time of the Messenger (ﷺ), adhered to a sacred law, such as the Jews and Christians. There is nothing to prevent that it means every community that worshipped, whether their traces remain or not, because His words ﴿they perform it﴾ are like a description of the communities, even if they are not worshipping at present.

As for His words ﴿So let them not dispute with you over the matter﴾, it is read as ﴿*falā yanziʿunnaka*﴾ (so let them not draw you away), meaning: remain firm in your religion with a steadfastness such that they do not hope to deceive you into removing you from it. As for His words ﴿So let them not dispute with you﴾, there are two views. One of them, which is the view of al-Zajjaj, is that it is a prohibition addressed to them against disputing with him, just as one says, "Let so-and-so not strike you," meaning, "Do not strike him." The second is that the intended meaning is that it is incumbent upon them to follow you and to abandon opposing you, since the matter is now settled upon your law and upon its abrogating all that is other than it. It is as if He, the Exalted, forbade every community that had any remnant remaining to continue in that custom, and obliged them to turn to following the Messenger (ﷺ). Therefore He said: ﴿and invite to your Lord﴾, meaning: do not limit the invitation to one community rather than another, for all of them are your community, so invite them to your law. ﴿Indeed you are upon a straight guidance.﴾ The word *hudā* (guidance) may mean the religion itself, or it may mean the proofs of the religion, and the latter is preferable. It is as if He said: invite them to this religion, for you, in terms of the indication of a clear path, are upon it. For this reason He said: ﴿And if they argue with you﴾, meaning: if they turn away from considering these proofs and resort to the method of obstinacy and clinging to custom, then you have made clear and manifested what is incumbent upon you. ﴿Then say: "Allah knows best what you do."﴾ This is because after the clarification of the proofs there remains only this kind of speech, which takes the place of a warning and an admonition about the judgment of the Day of Resurrection, which oscillates between Paradise and reward for those who accept, and between Fire and punishment for those who reject and deny. So He said: ﴿Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which you used to differ﴾, whereupon you will know the truth from falsehood. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 22, verses 71–72:

Page 58

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows whatever is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed, that is in a Book. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.﴾ ﴿And they worship besides Allah that for which He has sent down no authority and that of which they have no knowledge. And for the wrongdoers there will be no helper.﴾ ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, you recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve the denial. They nearly assault those who recite to them Our verses. Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve; and wretched is the destination."﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, said earlier: ﴿Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection﴾, He followed it with that by which it is known that He, glorified is He, knows what each one of them deserves, so that the judgment between them proceeds from Him with justice and not with injustice. So He said to His Messenger: ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows whatever is in the heaven and the earth?﴾ And here there are issues:

The first issue: His saying, ﴿Do you not know﴾, is in the form of a question, but its meaning is to strengthen the heart of the Messenger ﷺ, to give him the promise, and to warn the disbelievers that all their deeds are preserved with Allah; He does not go astray nor forget.

The second issue: The address is to the Messenger ﷺ, and what is meant is all of the servants. Because prophethood is not established except after knowledge that He, exalted is He, knows all the known things; for if that were not established, it would be possible that the liar be confused with the truthful, and then the manifestation of a miracle would not be a proof of truthfulness. And if that is so, it is impossible that the Messenger not know that. Thus it is established that what is meant is that it is an address to others.

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed, that is in a Book﴾, there are two opinions. The first, which is the view of Abu Muslim, is that the meaning of "Kitab" is preservation, safeguarding, and binding. It is said: "I sewed the waterskin (kataba al-mazadah)," when I stitch it, and thereby I preserve what is in it. Its meaning and the meaning of "Kitab" among people is the preservation of what they deal with. So what is meant by His saying, ﴿Indeed, that is in a Book﴾, is that it is preserved with Him. **Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 22, verse 73:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, a parable is coined, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gather together for it. And if the fly should snatch away from them anything, they could not retrieve it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought.﴾ ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure. Indeed, Allah is Strong, Mighty.﴾

Know that when He, glorified is He, had previously made clear that they worship besides Allah what has no proof or knowledge for them, He mentioned in this verse what indicates the nullification of their claim.

[Page 60]

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿a parable is coined﴾, there are questions concerning it.

The first question: What he brought is not a parable (mathal), so how did He call it a parable? The answer: Since a parable is, for the most part, a striking and strange remark, it is permissible to call anything that is like this a parable.

The second question: His saying ﴿is coined (ḍuriba)﴾ indicates a past action, while Allah, exalted is He, is the one who speaks this speech initially? The answer: If the description being presented was already known beforehand, then it is permissible for this to apply to it, and its mention is like repeating a matter that has already preceded.

As for His saying ﴿so listen to it (fastami'u lahu)﴾, that is: reflect upon it with its true reflection, because mere hearing does not benefit, and only reflection benefits. Know that since the fly is in the utmost weakness, Allah, exalted is He, used it as an argument for nullifying their claim in two respects.

The first: His saying ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gather together for it﴾. It is read "yad'ūna" with the ya' and with the ta', and "yud'awna" in the passive form. ''Lan'' (never) is basically for negating the future, except that it negates it emphatically. So it is as if He, glorified is He, said: Indeed these idols, even if they gather together, will never be able to create a fly, despite its weakness; so how is it fitting for the rational person to make them an object of worship? So His saying ﴿even if they gather together for it﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), as if He said: It is impossible for them to create a fly while they are gathered together, so how about when they are alone?

The second: His saying ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them anything, they could not retrieve it from it﴾ is as if He, glorified is He, said: I will leave aside the matter of creation and origination and speak about what is easier than that. For if the fly snatches something from them, they are not able to retrieve that thing from the fly. Know that the first proof is suitable to be relied upon in negating that the Messiah and the angels are gods. As for the second, it is not. If it is said: This argument either serves to negate that the idols are creators, knowing, living, and governing, or it serves to negate that they deserve veneration. The first is invalid, because the negation of their being like that is known necessarily, so what benefit is there in establishing a proof for it? As for the second: this proof does not establish it, because the negation of their being living does not necessitate that they not be venerated, for the aspects of veneration differ. The people believed about them that they were talismans placed in the form of the stars, or that they were images of the angels and of the earlier prophets, and they venerated them on the basis that their veneration necessitates the veneration of the angels and those earlier prophets. The answer: As for their being talismans placed upon the stars in such a way that harm and benefit come from them, this is refuted by this proof, for since they did not benefit themselves in this measure, namely rescuing themselves from a fly, then not benefiting others is even more fitting. As for their being images of the angels and of the earlier prophets, it has been established by reason that venerating other than Allah, exalted is He, should be less than venerating Allah, exalted is He. The people venerated them to the utmost degree, and in that case it would necessitate equating them with the Creator, glorified is He, in veneration. From here they became deserving of blame and reproach.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Weak are the seeker and the sought﴾, there are two opinions concerning it. One: What is meant by it is the idol and the fly. The idol is like the seeker in that, if it sought to create it and to retrieve from it what it had snatched, it would be unable to do so, and the fly is in the position of the sought. The second: The seeker is the one who worships the idol, and the sought is the idol itself or its worship. This is closer, because the idol's being a seeker is not literal but rather by way of supposition, whereas here it is by way of verification; yet there is a metaphor in it, since an idol cannot validly be weak, because weakness is only possible for one who can be strong. There is also a third aspect: that the meaning of His saying ﴿weak (ḍa'ufa)﴾ is not in terms of strength, but rather to make manifest the ugliness of this doctrine, just as one says to a person during debate: How weak this doctrine is, and how weak this argument is.

[p. 61]

As for His saying, ﴿They have not measured God with His true measure﴾, meaning: they did not magnify Him with the magnification due to Him, in that they made these idols, in the utmost of their baseness, partners with Him in divinity. This statement is explained in Surat al-An'am. He is "Strong" (Qawiyy), nothing is impossible for Him to do, and He is "Mighty" (Aziz), no one can overpower Him, so what need is there to say there is a partner?

Al-Kalbi said: Regarding this verse and its counterpart in Surat al-An'am, it was revealed concerning a group of Jews: Malik ibn al-Sayf, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, Ka'b ibn Asad, and others, may God curse them. They said that when God, glorified is He, finished creating the heavens and the earth, He became weary of their creation, so He lay down, rested, and placed one of His legs over the other. So this verse was revealed refuting them, and His saying, may He be exalted, was revealed: ﴿And We did not feel any fatigue﴾ [Qaf: 38].

Know that the source of these doubts is the belief in anthropomorphism (tashbih, ascribing likeness to created beings). It is therefore obligatory to declare God's Essence free from resemblance to other essences, contrary to what the Mushabbiha (anthropomorphists) say; to declare His attributes free from resemblance to other attributes, contrary to what the Karramiyya say; and to declare His acts free from resemblance to other acts, that is, purpose, motive, and deserving praise or blame, contrary to what the Mu'tazila say. The Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Ansari, may God have mercy on him, said: He, glorified is He, is majestic in description and mighty in attribute. Imaginations cannot picture Him, thoughts cannot determine Him, intellects cannot represent Him, times cannot encompass Him, and directions cannot contain or limit Him. He is Samad (self-sufficient, eternal) in His Essence and everlasting in His attributes.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 22, verses 75–76:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.﴾ ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾

Know that when He, glorified is He, had mentioned what pertains to divinity (al-ilahiyyat, matters concerning the Divine), He mentioned here what pertains to prophethood (al-nubuwwat, the institution of prophecy). Muqatil said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira said, "Was the Reminder sent down to him from among us?" So Allah, exalted is He, sent down this verse. Here there are two questions.

The first question: the word "min" (from among) indicates partitiveness (al-tab'id, partial sense). His saying ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels﴾ requires that the messengers be some of them, not all of them. But His saying ﴿who made the angels messengers﴾ requires that all of them be messengers, so a contradiction arises. The answer: what is meant here may be those who were messengers to the children of Adam, namely the greatest of the angels, such as Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, Izra'il, and the guardian angels (al-hafazah), may the blessings of Allah be upon them. As for all the angels, some of them are messengers to others, and thus the contradiction disappears.

The second question: He said in surah al-Zumar: ﴿Had Allah wished to take a son, He would have chosen whatever He willed from what He creates﴾ [al-Zumar: 4]. This indicates that any son must be one who is chosen. This verse indicates that some of the angels and some of mankind are among those chosen. Thus, taken together, the two verses would necessitate affirming a son. The answer: His saying ﴿Had Allah wished to take a son, He would have chosen﴾ indicates that every son is chosen, but it does not indicate that every chosen one is a son. Therefore, from the indication of this verse that there exist chosen ones, it does not follow that they are sons. There is another aspect of this verse: that its purpose is to rebuke those among the angels who were worshipped besides Allah. As if He, glorified is He, in the first verse refuted the saying of the idol-worshippers, and in this verse refuted the saying of the worshippers of the angels. He made clear that the high rank of the angels is not because they are gods, but because Allah, exalted is He, chose them on account of their worship. It is as if He, exalted is He, made clear that they did not measure Allah with His due measure when they made the angels objects of worship alongside Allah. Then He, glorified is He, made clear by His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾ that He hears what they say and sees what they do. For this reason He followed it with His saying ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾. Some said: what is before them and what is behind them refers to what preceded in this world and what came after. Others said: ﴿what is before them﴾ refers to the matters of the Hereafter, and ﴿what is behind them﴾ refers to the matters of this world. Then He followed it with His saying ﴿and to Allah all matters are returned﴾. So His saying ﴿He knows what is before them﴾ points to complete knowledge, and His saying ﴿and to Allah all matters are returned﴾ points to complete power, sole possession of divinity, and judgment. Together, these two contain the utmost deterrent against proceeding to disobedience.
